rounds.text: Amal Ltd is trading at a significant discount to its intrinsic value, with a discounted cash flow model indicating an intrinsic value of ₹ 989 per share against its current market price of ₹ 565, providing a substantial margin of safety of 42.9% [E41, E42]. The market price implies a modest 10.3% earnings growth, which sits well below the 18.0% growth assumed in the base case [E43]. Furthermore, the business is exceptionally well-financed with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x, borrowings at ₹ 0 Cr, and a comfortable current ratio of 2.48x [E34, E35, E36]. Operational execution remains robust, evidenced by a 51% compounded sales growth over 5 years, a 97% growth over the trailing twelve months, and profits fully backed by cash with a 1.00x cash conversion [E14, E16, E31]. Capital expenditure is largely complete with capital work-in-progress down by 66.7%, pointing to new capacity coming online alongside two evaluated growth projects [E37, E57]. Conceded: operating margins have faced recent pressure with TTM margins dropping to 11% and quarterly margins falling to 6% in Sep 2026, alongside a -23% decline in TTM compounded profit growth [E19, E27, E28].

Despite clean debt metrics, Amal Ltd carries significant valuation and operational risks that are not adequately supported by the evidence. The company trades at a P/E of 23.58x against a sector benchmark of 20.78x and an EV/EBITDA of 14.25x compared to its sector benchmark of 3.6x [E6, E11]. Furthermore, the stock sits at just 23% of its 52-week range while facing severe margin compression [E5, E27, E28]. Operating margins have dropped to 11% in the TTM from 18% three years prior, and quarterly operating margins plunged to 6% in September 2026 compared to 16% in the year-ago quarter [E27, E28]. This deterioration coincides with a 23% decline in compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and explicit warnings that earnings growth is decelerating [E19, E55]. Conceded: the company maintains a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x, robust short-term liquidity with a current ratio of 2.48x, and strong multi-year compounded sales growth [E34, E35, E14, E15, E16]. Nevertheless, month-to-month volatility in the price of key raw material sulphur presents a persistent operational cost headwind that threatens profitability as margins continue to contract [E64, E67].

Conceded: the P/E and EV/EBITDA multiples trade above general sector benchmarks [E6, E11]. However, the bear's focus on margin compression overlooks the overwhelming top-line momentum, where compounded sales growth reached 51% over 5 years, 58% over 3 years, and 97% in the trailing twelve months [E14, E15, E16]. Regarding the 52-week range low of 23%, this depressed price level sits alongside a compelling DCF-derived intrinsic value of ₹989 per share and a massive 42.9% margin of safety [E5, E41, E42]. Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth declined by 23% [E19]. Yet, the company is fundamentally sound with zero debt (0.00x debt-to-equity and ₹0 borrowings) and strong cash generation, including ₹22 crore in operating cash flow and ₹15 crore in free cash flow [E32, E33, E34, E36]. Finally, the backward-looking margin concerns ignore the positive operational turnaround signals, such as results scoring 71/100 and net profit up 2% YoY, confirming that stale sentiment should not overshadow improving business fundamentals [E53, E56].

Conceded: the company maintains zero debt, a comfortable current ratio of 2.48x, and generates positive operating and free cash flows [E32, E33, E34, E35]. However, the bull's reliance on top-line momentum ignores severe profitability deterioration, specifically a 23% decline in trailing twelve-month profit growth and an operating margin collapse of 7 percentage points over three years and 9 percentage points in the most recent quarter [E19, E27, E28]. While the bull highlights a large discount to an intrinsic value estimate, the rules-based screen explicitly flags that earnings growth is decelerating and notes that the stock sits only 23% of the way up its 52-week range [E5, E41, E55]. Conceded: past sales growth figures are high [E14, E15, E16], but these explosive top-line gains have failed to protect margins, which the filed statements categorize as inconsistent over both yearly and quarterly periods [E29, E30]. Finally, the valuation multiples remain elevated relative to sector benchmarks, with a P/E of 23.58x, a P/B of 4.97x, and an EV/EBITDA of 14.25x significantly outpacing their respective sector averages [E6, E7, E11].
